newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit up on short covering,.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit up on short covering,.

text.p: Most CME lumber contracts ended up the daily $10.00 per thousand board feet limit on heavy short covering and talk of limited exports from Canada, CME floor traders said.
November lumber expires this month and is currently trading without limits. The contract ended up a dramatic $27.00 per tbf at $449.00, traders noted.
"I've been down here nearly twenty years and that is the biggest single-day gain that I can remember," one trader said.
The pool of buy orders in January was estimated at 280 contracts and there were 50 contracts in March, sources said.
All contracts except November will have regular limits on Monday, according to the CME.
Talk that Canadian mills have far outsold their export quotas provided some of the momentum for the sharp rally in futures, floor traders said.
On Thursday, the Canadian government was said to have released quarterly softwood export allocations to Canadian lumber companies.
January lumber settled up $10.00 at $394.40 per tbf and March closed up $10.00 at $383.90. Other months were up $9.40 to $10.00 per tbf.
